messages:
lee: quick thread: when we failover from Dedicated -> Hosted were losing the `operator`/`pool_id` metadata and billing/latency charts get noisy. who owns preserving that meta?
mara: are we sure it's lost at the routing layer vs stripped by hosted ingress? saw both behaviors. :mag:
juan: hosted ingress currently canonicalizes a tenant id and drops unknown headers. we did that to avoid header spoofing.
anika: we need the metadata for eviction priority and SLO tagging. without it hosted moves traffic into default QoS and pages SREs.
rory: two orthogonal fixes: 1) routing attaches an internal header (fast), 2) sign a tiny lease-claim token that travels with the request (portable).
lee: pros/cons?
mara: internal header is easiest: route-proxy adds `x-rw-lease-meta: base64(...)` and we make sure frontdoor preserves it. downside: cross-cloud proxies or partner hops may drop it.
juan: signed token is stronger. controlplane issues lease token v2 with claims: {sub, pool_id, operator, eviction_priority, iat, exp, nonce}. hosted validates signature. can be verified without trusting every proxy.
anika: security note: must be short TTL and single-use nonce to avoid replay. also, hosted shouldn't accept arbitrary CAs unless in private mode.
rory: for private deployments, customers may run their own controlplane. plan: accept tokens signed by customer CA (opt-in) or require rotation via shared trust bundle in manifest. documented in private onboarding.
lee: telemetry: ensure we propagate `traceparent` + `redwood.operator` so metrics and traces map to original pool. otherwise billing reconciliation breaks.
mara: add audit entries whenever routing attaches meta: `audit.event=fallback_attached`, include original_pool and requester. keep logs for 90d.
juan: implement compatibility layers: short-term header-attach gate behind feature flag `routing.propagate_meta`. long-term token v2 with validation and a fallback `legacy_priority_mapper` that guesses priority from recent tenant behavior if claims absent.
anika: testing: add e2e handshake tests in infra/handshake-tests: simulate dedicated full -> fallback -> hosted and assert operator present in metrics and logs. also fuzz header-dropping scenarios.
rory: ops/runbook: how to revoke tokens or invalidate keys if controlplane is compromised. add key-revocation endpoint and publish CRL to hosted validation service.
lee: responsibilities: routing team owns header-attach RFC and quick patch; auth team owns token v2 design and signing; hosted / ingress team owns validation + legacy mapper; infra owns tests + runbook.
mara: timeline proposal: quick patch (header attach + log) in 2w, token v2 design + proto lib in 4w, hosted validation + rollout in 6-8w.
juan: small implementation detail: token should use JWS compact format, include nonce and be accepted only once (we track nonce in eviction-store with short TTL).
anika: nonces require store churn — maybe use HMAC with short exp and include `kid` for rotation to avoid per-token DB. tradeoff: can't single-use then. pick >60s TTL and short replay window.
rory: agree, prefer short TTL + nonce optional; we'll incrementally harden to single-use if needed.
infra-bot: Note: Incident 2024-04-03 logged fallback_attrib_gap. Remediation suggested: header-attach interim.
lee: action items summary:
- routing: implement header attach behind flag (mara)
- auth: draft token v2 claims + JWS prototype (juan)
- hosted: validation + legacy_priority_mapper (anika)
- infra: handshake e2e + header-drop fuzz (rory)
- security: revoke/rotation runbook (lee)
please ack ownership here.
mara: ack, will open PR and feature flag.
juan: ack, starting prototype today.
anika: ack, will add mapper sketch to hosted README.
rory: ack, will add tests and a small chaos job to drop headers across infra.
lee: thanks all. syncing Fri 10:30 to check progress, i'll post a short RFC summary to #architecture and ping eng-sre.
